sentences.text:
This petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed seeking the following reliefs :-
"i)To call for the relevant record pertaining to the subject matter for kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court.
ii)To issue a writ in the nature of Mandamus directing the learned Second District Judge Devsar Distt:
Singrauli M.P. to adjudicate the reference case dt. 28.2.22 filed by the petitioner within specific period under the provisions of Section 51(1) (2) and section 64 of Land Acquisition and Rehabilitation Adhinium as per Ann.P/1.
iii) Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of this case may also be passed together cost of the petition."
2.
It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner has filed a Civil Suit No.200218A/2016 for declaration of title and permanent injunction.
In spite of the injunction order, the compensation of the land in dispute was received by the private respondents.

The petitioner has filed a reference case under section 64 of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 2013"), which is pending before the Second District Judge, Devsar, District Singrauli with no further development in the same Dadai Sahu vs Rajmani Sahu on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90450846/

sentences.text:
3. Considered the submissions made in the writ petition.
4.
The petition has been drafted in a vague manner.
The date of passing of award by the L.A.O. has not been clarified.

The application under section 64 of Act, 2013 has to be filed before the Collector,
who will make reference to the concerning authority.

However, it appears that without approaching the Collector, Singrauli, the petitioner has directly filed a reference under section 64 of Act, 2013 before the Second Additional District Judge, Singrauli.
The petitioner has not filed the copy of the proceedings of the Court of Second Additional District Judge, Devsar, District Singrauli.

entities.text: Court of Second Additional District Judge, Devsar, District Singrauli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
5. The Supreme Court in the case of High Court Bar Association, Allahabad Vs. State of U.P. and Others decided on 29.02.2024 in Criminal Appeal No.3589/2023 has held as under :-
"32.

entities.text: High Court Bar Association, Allahabad Vs. State of U.P. and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, constitutional Courts should not normally fix a time-bound schedule for disposal of cases pending in any Court.
The pattern of pendency of various categories of cases pending in every Court, including High Courts, is different.
The situation at the grassroots level is better known to the judges of the concerned Courts.
Therefore, the issue of giving out-of-turn priority to certain cases should be best left to the concerned Courts.

The orders fixing the outer limit for the disposal of cases should be passed only in exceptional circumstances to meet extraordinary situations."
6.

Since nothing has been pointed out by the petitioner to show that who is responsible for delay,
therefore, it is clear that the petitioner has not pointed out any exceptional circumstance warranting direction to the trial court.
7.
Accordingly, no case is made out warranting interference.
8. The petition fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE TG/-
